## govern

`github.com/bide-ai/bide/govern` · [pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/bide-ai/bide/govern) · Stability: **experimental**

Package govern is the Tier-2 (distributed / concurrent) compensating-agent layer: it integrates the gsm "Governed State Machine" library so that MULTIPLE concurrent agents mutating SHARED state converge to the same valid state regardless of interleaving, as certified by gsm's build-time normalization-confluence verification (WFC + CC).

**Functions**

- `func EventTool(gov Applier, cfg EventToolConfig) agent.Tool`: EventTool gives an agent a GOVERNED action: when the agent's LLM calls it, cfg.Event is applied to the shared governed state (convergent + thread-safe).
- `func FederatedEventTool(gov FederatedApplier, cfg FederatedEventToolConfig) agent.Tool`: FederatedEventTool gives an agent a GOVERNED federated action: when the agent's LLM calls it, cfg.Event is applied to component cfg.Registry of the shared federation.
- `func QuorumConfigStep(name string) string`: QuorumConfigStep is the step name under which the quorum named name records its k and voters.
- `func QuorumTallyStep(name string) string`: QuorumTallyStep is the step name of the tally of the quorum named name.
- `func QuorumVoteStep(name, voter string) string`: QuorumVoteStep is the step name of voter's vote in the quorum named name.


ConfluenceCertificate is the machine-checkable evidence that a governed policy converges, carried out of gsm's build-time verification and into the SDK so it can be surfaced to a user and anchored in the audit trail.

**Constructors and functions**

- `func CertifyConvergence(rep *gsm.Report, policyDigest string) ConfluenceCertificate`: CertifyConvergence translates a gsm build Report and the policy's digest into a portable certificate.

**Methods**

- `func (c ConfluenceCertificate) Classification() string`: Classification names the fragment the machine lives in, for a human-facing report.
- `func (c ConfluenceCertificate) Marshal() ([]byte, error)`: Marshal serializes the certificate for anchoring as an audit leaf (see audit.RecordConvergence).
- `func (c ConfluenceCertificate) String() string`: String renders the certificate for a build log or CLI.

### type FederatedGovernor

```go
type FederatedGovernor struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

FederatedGovernor is a governor over a gsm federation (multiple component registries linked by directed morphisms), backed by a shared, durable EventLog.

**Constructors and functions**

- `func NewFederated(ctx context.Context, m *gsm.FedMachine, log EventLog, entity string, initial gsm.FedState) (*FederatedGovernor, error)`: NewFederated constructs a federated governor over the entity's log and reconstructs its state by replaying the log from the initial federated state.

**Methods**

- `func (fg *FederatedGovernor) Apply(ctx context.Context, registry, event string) (FedApplied, error)`: Apply validates the (registry, event) against the federation, appends it to the shared log, then folds the log into the state up to and including its position.
- `func (fg *FederatedGovernor) ApplyOnce(ctx context.Context, id, registry, event string) (FedApplied, error)`: ApplyOnce is Apply at most once per id, across every process sharing the log (see FederatedApplier).
- `func (fg *FederatedGovernor) State() gsm.FedState`: State returns the governor's view of the federated state as of its last Apply or Sync.
- `func (fg *FederatedGovernor) Sync(ctx context.Context) (gsm.FedState, error)`: Sync folds every entry the log currently holds into the state and returns it, so the governor reflects other processes' events without applying one of its own.


Governor applies agents' events to one in-memory, gsm-governed state.

**Constructors and functions**

**Methods**

- `func (g *Governor) Apply(_ context.Context, event string) (Applied, error)`: Apply advances the shared state by one event (O(1) table lookup; compensation to a valid normal form is baked in).
- `func (g *Governor) ApplyOnce(_ context.Context, id, event string) (Applied, error)`: ApplyOnce is Apply at most once per id (see Applier).
- `func (g *Governor) State() gsm.State`: State returns the current shared normal-form state.

### type PersistentGovernor

```go
type PersistentGovernor struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

PersistentGovernor is a governor over a shared, durable EventLog.

**Constructors and functions**

- `func NewPersistent(ctx context.Context, m *gsm.Machine, log EventLog, entity string, initial gsm.State) (*PersistentGovernor, error)`: NewPersistent constructs a governor over the entity's log and reconstructs its state by replaying the log from the initial state.

**Methods**

- `func (pg *PersistentGovernor) Apply(ctx context.Context, event string) (Applied, error)`: Apply appends the event to the shared log, then folds the log into the state up to and including the event's position (so every earlier event, from any process, is applied first, in log order), and returns that state and position.
- `func (pg *PersistentGovernor) ApplyOnce(ctx context.Context, id, event string) (Applied, error)`: ApplyOnce is Apply at most once per id (see Applier), across every process sharing the log: the id travels with the append, and the log records each id once.
- `func (pg *PersistentGovernor) State() gsm.State`: State returns the governor's view of the shared state as of its last Apply or Sync.
- `func (pg *PersistentGovernor) Sync(ctx context.Context) (gsm.State, error)`: Sync folds every event the log currently holds into the state and returns it, so the governor reflects other processes' events without applying one of its own.

## govern/eventlogtest

`github.com/bide-ai/bide/govern/eventlogtest` · [pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/bide-ai/bide/govern/eventlogtest) · Stability: **experimental**

Package eventlogtest checks that an implementation satisfies the govern.EventLog contract, so every adapter (in-memory, SQLite, Postgres, Redis, or your own) is held to the same guarantees a governor relies on: dense, unique positions under concurrent appends from separate processes, appends that are idempotent by id (so a retried append is recorded once), and a log that only ever grows at the end.

**Functions**

- `func Run(t *testing.T, open func(t *testing.T) govern.EventLog)`: Run runs the conformance suite.
